status: EXISTS — the OMS owns the source; the verbatim copy lives in contracts/oms-mediabuyer.v1/ (hash-pinned by tests/oms-contract.test.ts). This file adds the ADD items and the cross-references, nothing that changes the copy.
direction: PULL — the media buyer calls the OMS: real orders, the spend per ad, stock. Two ADD calls go the other way round (the media buyer asks the OMS to send a Telegram message; the OMS sends the media buyer a signed «اوقف» event).

auth.rule: OAuth 2.1 + PKCE, exactly like the media buyer's own /mcp connector (reference implementation, public: src/core/oauth.ts + src/server/oauth.ts in the media buyer repo). The system that OWNS the data is the authorization server; the owner presses «اربط ← اسمح» once; nobody copies a token. The Bearer header on each call is unchanged.

endpoints.authorize: GET /oauth/authorize (the owner is logged in to that system and approves)
endpoints.token: POST /oauth/token (authorization_code + code_verifier S256, refresh_token with rotation)

auth.lifetimes: access token about one hour; refresh token about 60 days, rotated on every use; a revoked client or grant is refused on the very next call
auth.refused: a redirect address that was not registered, a missing or wrong PKCE verifier, a code used twice
auth.status: ADD — on the authorization server's side (small if it copies the reference implementation; additive; the old per-system keys can keep working until the owner switches)
auth.replaces: the pasted OMS_TOKEN: the key minted in OMS Settings → Apps → «توكنات الأنظمة» stays valid until the owner presses «اربط ← اسمح», then it can be revoked
auth.resource_server: the existing /api/v1 door (scopes are the existing ones); Bearer on every call
auth.scopes_note: capi.identifiers is no longer requested (decision of 17/11): the OMS sends the custom conversions (ConfirmedOrder / DeliveredOrder) itself, so no customer identifier ever has to move to the media buyer.

rate_limit: 30 calls per minute on the media buyer's key (429 RATE_LIMITED)
idempotency: Reads need none. The CAPI identifiers POST is a pure read: the same refs always answer the same.

endpoints.change: Let the OMS be the authorization server for its own /api/v1 door: a consent screen («الميديا باير بدّه يقرا الطلبات والمنتجات — اسمح؟») that issues the same kind of scoped, per-company token the door already checks (system = mediabuyer), with expiry and refresh. Replaces minting and pasting a key.
endpoints.size: small — it reuses the door's existing token table and scopes; the reference implementation is public

query.updated_since: ISO-8601 with offset, required, at most 31 days back

endpoints.pagination: cursor: {items, next_cursor}; the media buyer stops at 100 pages or when a cursor repeats

errors.when: updated_since missing or older than 31 days

endpoints.notes: Status words are six: new · confirmed · shipped · delivered · returned · canceled (the OMS maps its 14 core states onto them). `ad_id` is what joins an order to an ad: it must be filled for landing-page orders (see ADD A2 and the Pages contract).

query.fields: comma list from products-page.schema.json: code,name,aliases,unit_cost_usd,price_options,stock_days,delivery_fee,return_fee,cod_fee_pct (+ ADD A3: stock_units,daily_sales_7d)

endpoints.notes: A figure the OMS has no single source for is null, never a guess. A null never wipes a number the owner typed in the media buyer's settings.

endpoints.status: EXISTS — FROZEN, NOT USED BY THE MEDIA BUYER from 17/11
endpoints.notes: Kept as published (a published version never breaks) but the media buyer does not call it and does not ask for its scope: the OMS already sends the server-side custom conversions to Meta for confirmed and delivered orders, and building them twice would double-count. The media buyer's own conversion sender stays off (its queue is not drained).

endpoints.change: Accept and store the ad tags in the body's `attribution` object (optional fields, shape-checked, ids digits only): adset_id, campaign_id, ad_name, utm_source, utm_medium, fbclid, fbc, fbp, landing_url. `ad_id` already exists there. Return them on /orders/attribution as ad_id, adset_id, campaign_id, ad_name, landing_page (those fields are already in the frozen schema). fbc/fbp/fbclid are sealed like the other identifiers and only ever leave through capi/identifiers.
endpoints.size: small — optional fields on an existing object; an order without them is accepted exactly as before

query.date_to: YYYY-MM-DD, required, at most 31 days after date_from

endpoints.pagination: cursor: {items, next_cursor}; ordered by date then ad_id so a page never repeats a row
endpoints.change: Expose, read-only and by scope `ad_spend.read`, the daily spend the OMS already pulls from Meta (system-user token, the account's 145 campaigns). One row per day per ad (or adset / campaign by `level`). Money is a decimal string in the account's currency; a figure the OMS does not hold is null, never 0. The media buyer's own Meta token is for WRITES only and is never used to read the spend that decides a cost per order.

as_of.description: when the OMS last pulled from Meta (ISO-8601 with offset); a stale as_of is shown to the owner as «قديم», not hidden

errors.when: a date is missing or malformed, or the window is over 31 days

endpoints.size: small — a read over the table the spend sync already fills

endpoints.change: Make `stock_days` non-null whenever the OMS holds a stock count: stock_units ÷ daily_sales_7d (units shipped in the last 7 days ÷ 7). Add the two inputs as optional fields so the media buyer can show them and check the division.
endpoints.size: small — two optional columns on an existing read

endpoints.change: The OMS is the ONE Telegram gateway for every system (it already has the bot and the webhook). The media buyer holds no bot token: it asks the OMS to deliver a message. The OMS decides the transport, the language and the topic.

key.description: idempotency key: the same key sends once (24 hours)

example_request.text: طلب جديد: هوكات جديدة — TRF01 / JOB-12

errors.when: an unknown person key or a chat the bot is not in
the text looks like a phone number or an address (refused, not sent)
Telegram did not accept it (the message is not lost: retry with the same key)

endpoints.notes: Telegram is blocked in Jordan and not on the server: the OMS server sends. A message from the media buyer never carries a customer detail. «owner» = the owner's private chat; `person` = a key of the media buyer's team directory the OMS maps to a chat.
endpoints.size: small — one endpoint over the OMS's own Telegram sender

headers.X-Zaki-Timestamp: unix seconds (rejected if more than 5 minutes old)
headers.X-Zaki-Signature: sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of «<timestamp>.<raw body>» with the signing secret>

endpoints.change: When the owner writes «اوقف …» to the bot, the OMS (which owns the bot and the webhook) forwards it to the media buyer as a SIGNED event — the same signed-outbox shape as contracts/oms-app-events.v1. The media buyer turns it into the same safety ChangeSet it makes today (pause only; anything that spends is refused with a link to the site). The signing secret comes back once in the OAuth token response (`event_signing_secret`) — never pasted.

example_response.reply: وقّفت CR00147 — بتقدر ترجّعه من بانتظارك

errors.when: bad or missing signature, or an old timestamp

endpoints.notes: The OMS may show `reply` back to the owner through its own bot. The media buyer's own Telegram webhook is retired once this is live. Money is never approved from here: a request to spend answers with a link to the site.
endpoints.size: small on the OMS (one signed delivery); small on the media buyer (one route over the existing stop logic) — MEDIA BUYER ADD, not built yet

media_buyer.note: no token variable: «اربط ← اسمح» stores the token (encrypted) and refreshes it. META_SYSTEM_USER_TOKEN here is for WRITES to Meta only; spend is read from the OMS.

oms.APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY: (secret — already required there; without it fbc/fbp/fbclid are dropped, never stored clear)
oms.note: the OMS keeps its own Telegram bot (TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN lives ONLY there) and its own Meta system-user token (spend + the server-side custom conversions)

$comment: Written by the media buyer (docs/INTEGRATION_CONTRACTS.md). A published version never breaks: only optional fields are added; a removed, renamed or retyped field is v2. No customer name, phone or address in any field, under any name.
